paper.title: Distributed Online Bandit Nonconvex Optimization with One-Point Residual Feedback via Dynamic Regret

settings.name_in_paper: Constrained nonconvex distributed online bandit optimization (DOBO) over time-varying digraph
unmapped: regret is a first-order stationarity-based dynamic regret (sum of <grad f_k(x_jk), x_jk - x>)
n agents communicating over a time-varying, uniformly (U-)strongly connected balanced digraph with doubly stochastic weights
learner needs graph constants Gamma, gamma and number of agents n to set step size
one-point residual feedback: one function query per round, residual with previous query
settings.definition_quote: At round $k$ of the game, each player $i$ selects a decision $x_{i,k}$ from the convex set $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$... The adversary then assigns an arbitrary, possibly nonconvex, loss function $f_{i,k}$ to the player. In the bandit setting, players only observe specific loss values corresponding to their own decisions

settings.name_in_paper: Constrained convex DOBO over time-varying digraph
unmapped: n agents over time-varying balanced uniformly strongly connected digraph
learner needs graph constants Gamma, gamma and n for step size
settings.definition_quote: For the constrained convex DOBO problem (1), we introduce the expected dynamic network regret for an arbitrary node j: E-DR^cv_{j,T} = sum_k E[f_k(x_{j,k})] - sum_k E[f_k(x_k^*)]

algorithms.name: OP-DOPGD (distributed online projected gradient descent with one-point residual feedback)

bound.expression: Max(T**Max(a_s, 1 - b_s), T**(2*b_s - a_s)*Theta_T**2, T**(b_s - a_s)*Theta_T, T**a_s*omega_T**2)

conditions: Assumption 1: time-varying balanced digraph, doubly stochastic weights, U-strongly connected
Omega compact convex with diameter D
f_{i,k} L_0-Lipschitz and L_1-smooth on Omega
tuning: M = 4 sqrt(3d) n Gamma L_0 gamma/(1-gamma)

source.quote: Then, for any $T\ge1$ and $j\in \mathcal{V}$, the resulting dynamic regret satisfies: E-DR^ncv_{j,T} \le O(max{ T^{max{a,1-b}}, T^{2b-a}\Theta_T^2, T^{b-a}\Theta_T, T^a\omega_T^2 }).

results.notes: Regret is stationarity-based dynamic regret for nonconvex losses. Paper's statement of parameter constraints is muddled (0<=delta<=a-b; Lemma 5 uses 0<b<=a<1).

bound.regime: a = 1/2, delta_s in [0, 1/2), delta_s <= a - b

source.label: thm2
source.quote: Moreover, setting \(a = \frac{1}{2}\) yields an improved bound on the dynamic regret: E-DR \le O(max{T^{1/2+\delta},T^{1/2-2\delta}\Theta_T^2,T^{1/2}\omega_T^2}) for any $\delta \in [0, \frac{1}{2})$.

results.notes: The paper's delta here is an exponent, not a failure probability.

source.quote: In the specific case where $a = b $, the dynamic regret simplifies to $ \mathcal{O}(\max\{T^{1/2},T^{1/2}\Theta_{T}^2,T^{1/2}\omega_T^2 \})$.

results.notes: Theorem states a=b; proof uses a=b=1/2.

symbols.M_c: constant M = 4 sqrt(3d) n Gamma L_0 gamma/(1-gamma)

conditions: L_lip is the paper's L_0, N the number of agents n, diam_K the paper's D

source.label: convex
source.quote: Then, for all $T\ge1$ and $j\in \mathcal{V}$, the resulting dynamic regret satisfies E-DR^cv_{j,T} \le \{ nD^{2}M+2nD(d+3)^{3/2}+\frac{H_1}{2M}\}\sqrt{T} +nM\sqrt{T}\omega_T^2+2nDM\sqrt{T}\omega_T+\frac{H_2\sqrt{T}}{2M}\Theta_T^2+ \frac{H_3}{2M} \Theta_T

results.notes: Function-value dynamic regret for convex losses.
